intracellular pH changes the force of contraction in isolated rat portal vein by altering both the calcium sensitivity and the calcium‐activated force.
intracellular calcium release is not a major factor in the regulation of spontaneous force in rat portal vein.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the force of contraction of the rat portal vein is dependent on both extracellular and intracellular calcium pools and that these pools interact in a complex manner with the intracellular pH of the smooth muscle cell.

the spontaneous force of rat mesenteric portal vein is dependent on both extracellular and intracellular calcium, and that the relative contribution of each calcium source to force is dependent on intracellular pH.

the calcium entry pathway is the major source of calcium for the spontaneous contractile activity of portal vein and is also involved in the intracellular pH‐dependent changes in force.
calcium entry from outside is a necessary condition for intracellular pH‐dependent modulation of spontaneous mechanical activity of rat portal vein.
